chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Shami narrated to me, saying: A man in Syria, called Hilqam ibn Abi Hilqam, narrated to me, saying: I went to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him).
So I said to him: May I be your ransom, teach me a comprehensive supplication for the world and the Hereafter, and make it brief. He said: Say at the end of the Fajr prayer until the sun rises.
"Glorious is Allah the Magnificent, and by His praise I seek forgiveness of Allah, and I ask Him from His grace."

Hilqam said: I was in the worst state among my family members, and I did not know [why], until an inheritance came to me from a man whom I did not think had any kinship with me. And today I am among the wealthiest of my family, and that is not except due to what my master, the righteous servant (peace be upon him), taught me.

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: The righteous servant (title for Imam al-Sadiq)

ai.seo_question: What is the brief comprehensive supplication for worldly and spiritual success taught by the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribed this concise supplication for the time between the Fajr prayer and sunrise, emphasizing the power of brevity combined with sincerity. The narrator Hilqam attests that this specific practice transformed his financial standing from poverty to wealth, illustrating the practical efficacy of adhering to the teachings of the 'Abd al-Salih (the pious servant). This narration is frequently cited in Shia tradition to highlight the spiritual and material benefits of consistent dhikr during the early morning hours.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr who said, ‘Abu Ja’far Al Shamy narrated to me saying, ‘A man called Hilqam Bin Abu Hilqam narrated to me at Syria saying, 
‘I went over to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Teach me a comprehensive supplication for the world and the Hereafter, and be brief’.

So heasws said: ‘Say at the end of Al-Fajr (Salāt) up to the emergence of the sun, ‘Glorious is Allahazwj the Magnificent, and by Hisazwj Praise I seek Forgiveness of Allahazwj, and I ask Himazwj from Hisazwj Grace’’.

Hilqam (the narrator) said, ‘I had been in an evil state from my family members, until (one day) there came to me, an inheritance from a man who I did not think there was any relationship between me and him, and today I am from the most affluential people of my family, and that was not except due to what was taught to me by my Master<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, Al-Abd Al-Salih<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> (7<sup style="font-weight: normal">th</sup> Imam<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>)’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from m Mahziyar who has that narrated to h Imams abu la’ far al-Shami saying that narrated to him a man in al- Sham (Damascus) called Hilqamu ibn abu Hilqamu who said the following: “Once I went in the presence of abu Ibrahim, recipient of divine supreme covenant.

I said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, instruct me with a supplication of universal form for this world and hereafter but very short one.’ The Imam said, ‘After the morning-prayer until sunrise say, “Glory belongs to Allah, the Great and I praise Him. I plead before Allah for forgiveness and I beg of His generosity. ’ “

Hilqamu has said, ‘I (financially) was the worst off person in my family. I received an inheritance from a man whom I did not think was related to me and I had no knowledge, but today I am the most comfortable person among my people and this is only because of what my master, the virtuous servant (of Allah) instructed me with.’”
